tool.name: SURVIVOR merge
tool.description: structural variant calls from several callers or samples into one VCF

param.name: input_vcfs
param.label: VCF files to merge
param.help: Two or more SV callsets, one per caller or sample. A list collection works too. The order of the inputs sets the order of the sample columns and of the SUPP_VEC flags in the output.

param.name: distance_type
param.label: Maximum distance between breakpoints is given as
param.option: A fixed number of base pairs
A fraction of the SV length

param.name: max_distance_bp
param.label: Maximum distance between breakpoints (bp)
param.help: Start and end breakpoints of two calls must each lie within this distance for the calls to be merged.

param.name: max_distance_fraction
param.label: Maximum distance between breakpoints (fraction of SV length)
param.help: For example 0.1 allows the breakpoints of a 5 kb deletion to differ by 500 bp.

validator.message: Enter a value greater than 0 and less than 1

param.name: min_support
param.label: Minimum number of supporting inputs
param.help: A merged call is reported only if at least this many input VCFs contain it. Use 1 to keep the union of all calls.

param.name: same_type
param.label: Only merge calls of the same SV type
param.help: If disabled, for example a deletion and a duplication at the same breakpoints are merged.

param.name: same_strand
param.label: Only merge calls on the same strands

param.name: min_size
param.label: Minimum SV size (bp)
param.help: Only calls longer than this are reported.

tool.help:
## What it does
[SURVIVOR](https://github.com/fritzsedlazeck/SURVIVOR) merge combines structural variant (SV) calls from several VCF files into one VCF. It is typically used to build a consensus callset from several SV callers run on the same sample, or to merge callsets from several samples into a multi-sample VCF.
Two calls are merged when their start and end breakpoints both lie within the maximum distance and, optionally, when they have the same SV type and strands. A merged call is reported only if it is supported by at least the chosen number of input files.
## Inputs
Two or more VCF files (plain or bgzipped), one per caller or sample. A list collection works too.
Each input must have a single sample column. SURVIVOR keeps only one column per input and can fill it with another sample's genotype, so the tool stops with an error if an input has more than one. Split multi-sample VCFs first, for example with bcftools.
SURVIVOR reads the SV type and end from the `SVTYPE` and `END` (or `SVLEN`) INFO fields that most SV callers write. Callers with unusual VCF dialects, in particular for breakends (`BND`), may not be parsed correctly, so check the merged calls.
## Parameters
The defaults (1000 bp, 2 supporting inputs, same type, same strand, 30 bp minimum size) are the values used in the SURVIVOR documentation for building a consensus from several callers. SURVIVOR's option to estimate the distance from the SV size is disabled in its code, so it is not offered here.
- **Maximum distance between breakpoints**: either a fixed number of base pairs or a fraction (between 0 and 1) of the SV length. Breakpoints must be closer than this value, not equal to it. A fraction cannot apply to calls whose breakpoints are on different chromosomes, so SURVIVOR uses a fixed 1000 bp for those. - **Minimum number of supporting inputs**: 1 keeps every call (union), the number of inputs keeps only calls found in all of them (intersection). A value larger than the number of inputs gives a VCF with no calls. - **Only merge calls of the same SV type**: if disabled, calls of different types at the same breakpoints, for example a deletion and a duplication, are merged. - **Only merge calls on the same strands**: if disabled, calls are merged whatever their strands. - **Minimum SV size**: only calls longer than this are reported, so a call of exactly this size is dropped. Calls between chromosomes are not filtered by size.
## Output
A VCF with one sample column per input, in input order. Sample columns are named after the sample columns of the inputs, with a numeric suffix where names repeat. Useful INFO fields:
- `SUPP`: number of inputs that support the merged call. - `SUPP_VEC`: a string of 0 and 1, one character per input in input order, that shows which inputs support the call. `101` means the first and third input.
In the FORMAT fields, `ID` and `CO` give the original ID and coordinates of each input call. Inputs without the call get an empty (`./.`) entry.
